newsitem.title: UK: UK housing market strongest for eight years - RICS.
newsitem.headline: UK housing market strongest for eight years - RICS.

text.p: The housing market in England and Wales is expected to be stronger this autumn than it has been for eight years, the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) said in its latest survey.
"The unusually vigorous summer market persisted throughout August, with confidence spreading across the country," it said in its survey for the three months to the end of August.
A net balance of 37 percent of chartered surveyor estate agents reported rising residential property prices in August. The balance in London alone was 84 percent.
Stock levels fell further and the shortage of properties is continuing to push prices up.
"Growing optimism among home-owners was fuelled further by other economic factors such as falling unemployment, rising disposable income and low interest rates," the RICS said.

RICS housing market spokesman Ian Perry said the housing market's strength was self-fulfilling. "As prices rise, more people are beginning to make enquiries and put their homes on the market...The market has been improving now for 12 consecutive months. It is no longer a question of recovery, the improvement is definitely here to stay."
